newsitem.title: BELGIUM: CBR buys 60 pct of Polish aggregates firm.
newsitem.headline: CBR buys 60 pct of Polish aggregates firm.

text.p: Belgian cement company CBR said on Thursday it had acquired 60 percent of Polish aggregates company Zielonogorskie Kopalnie Surowcow Mineralnych (ZKSM) and would make an offer to ZKSM's minority shareholders for the remainder.
The acquistion, which is subject to clearance by Polish anti-trust authorities, was carried out by CBR's Polish Gorazde unit. Terms were not disclosed.
ZKSM's minority shareholders comprise the company's 850 employees and the Polish state.
In 1995, ZKSM sold 2.7 million tons of aggregates for 33.3 million zlotys, or around 315 million Belgian francs, CBR spokeswoman Catherine Alexandre told Reuters.
She said the aggregates business was small as a proportion of CBR's existing aggregates activities in other parts of Europe but were an important development in its Polish business.
The acquisition was part of a strategy to model CBR's Polish activities on those in western Europe, where cement, aggregates and ready mix concrete businesses are integrated vertically, she said.
"We already had the cement business. Now we have the aggregates and we hope to get the readymix," she said.
A ready mix business could be developed independently or also through an acquisition, she said.
CBR is controlled by German cement group Heidelberger Zement AG.
